summary: The gate is at the right rung (3), is wired, is not vacuous (it prints and the harness asserts the file count), and the module exemption is sound and narrow -- two files, and an `implements` carve-out would have been 11. But the literal-stripping runs in the wrong order, so a string containing `//` or a `/*`/`*/` pair blanks real code and hides a real violation; and the banned list omits java.io file I/O, java.util.Date/Calendar, NIO channels and URI.toURL entirely while AGENTS.md now flips non-negotiable 7 from 'No script yet' to 'enforced' with no blind spot stated -- gate-design step 5. Six compiled business-logic files reaching the real filesystem, the real clock and a real socket were MEASURED passing green.

findings.title: io_seam_scan.code_only strips comments BEFORE string literals, so a comment delimiter inside a string blanks real code and hides a real violation
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py:41-47 (code_only, the `for pattern in (BLOCK, LINE, STRING, CHAR)` loop)
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a throwaway worktree at the staged bytes, both files valid Java that compiles. (a) A line holding a URL string and a real call: `byte[] all(Path p) throws Exception { log("see https://x/y"); return Files.readAllBytes(p); }` -- the LINE regex `//[^\n]*` is applied while the string literal is still present, matches `//x/y"); return Files.readAllBytes(p); }` and blanks the rest of the line. The scanner reports NOTHING. (b) A file with `static final String OPEN = "/*";` on one line, `return Files.readAllBytes(p);` on the next, and `static final String CLOSE = "*/";` on the third -- BLOCK is `/\*.*?\*/` with re.S, matches across all three and blanks the violation between them. The scanner reports NOTHING. Both were run through `scripts/io_seam_scan.py` at the staged revision and both printed a count with no violation line. The fix is order: blank STRING and CHAR first, then BLOCK and LINE, or tokenise in one pass. The change's own javadoc calls this machinery 'pinned rather than assumed' (IoSeamGateTest.aBannedCallQUOTEDInAJavadocOrASTRINGIsNotAViolation), but that case's string is `"forbidden: Instant.now() and Files."` -- it never puts a comment delimiter inside a string, which is the one input the ordering gets wrong. This is the packet's named lens exactly: a gate printing `ok` over code it did not examine.

findings.title: The banned list covers no java.io file I/O, no java.util clock and no NIO channel, and no blind spot is stated anywhere -- while AGENTS.md now presents non-negotiable 7 as scripted
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py:13-31 (BANNED), AGENTS.md:150-155, docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md:19-26, backlog.md M0.107 State cell
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: six business-logic files were written under `ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/`, staged, compiled clean with javac, and `./scripts/check-io-seam.sh --full` reported `ok 107 business-logic file(s) take a seam for every clock, socket and store`, exit 0. They were: `new FileInputStream("/etc/hostname").readAllBytes()`; `new RandomAccessFile(new File("/var/lib/wal/seg"), "r").length()`; `new Date().getTime() + Calendar.getInstance().getTimeInMillis()`; `SocketChannel.open(new InetSocketAddress("peer", 9000))`; `URI.create("http://peer:9000/seg").toURL().openStream()`; and `Instant\n    .now()` split across two lines (the scan is per-line). The first of these is the SAME defect the task was opened for -- the M5.8 measurement was `Files.readAllBytes(Path.of("/etc/hostname"))` in the membership seam -- written the java.io way instead of the java.nio.file way, and the gate is silent. The task cell scopes the row to 'a static scan for `java.io`, `java.net`, `java.nio.file`, `Clock` and `Instant.now`': the deliberate `Clock` exclusion is argued well and I accept it, but `java.io` is uncovered with no argument and no mention, `java.net` is covered only by four `new X(` forms, and `java.nio.file` misses `FileSystems.getDefault().getPath`. Nothing in the script header, the two standards edits, or the State cell says what the gate cannot see. gate-design/SKILL.md step 5 requires exactly that -- 'State what it cannot see. A documented blind spot is worth more than an undocumented mechanism that half works' -- and AGENTS.md models the discipline for check-tdd in two long paragraphs. The harm is the flip from '*No script yet*' to '-> scripts/check-io-seam.sh': every future agent now reads non-negotiable 7 as enforced, which is the failure mode this row's own text warns about ('a one-off test here would ... make the absence look closed'). Either widen BANNED to the java.io/java.util/NIO-channel routes, or state the blind spot in the script header and in AGENTS.md alongside the arrow.

findings.title: Two false-refusal paths -- an identifier ending in `Files` and a Java text block -- and the gate-weakening pressure runs the direction non-negotiable 2 forbids
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py:28 (`('Files.', ...)` matched as a bare substring) and :37 (STRING excludes `\n`, so text blocks are never stripped)
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED at the staged bytes. (a) `int n(List<String> dataFiles) { return dataFiles.size(); }` is reported as `Files. reaches the filesystem directly`, because the needle is an unanchored substring. That shape is live in this tree today -- `binstore-backends/.../LocalFsBinStore.java:393` is `dataFiles.add(p);` -- and is spared only because that module is exempt; the first `segmentFiles`/`pendingFiles` local in ingest or sequencer reds the commit for nothing. (b) A Java text block `static final String DOC = """
  never call Files.readAllBytes from here
  """;` is reported as a violation: the STRING regex forbids `
` so it cannot match a text block, and the content lines are scanned as code. That is precisely the input the design says it handles -- the script header's stated reason for stripping at all is that 'this tree's comments quote code constantly'. gate-design step 3: 'A gate that rejects legitimate input gets switched off, and then it enforces nothing.' Anchor the needle (` Files\.` or require a non-identifier char before it) and strip `"""..."""` before the single-line STRING pass.

findings.title: The real-tree harness case derives its expected count from Files.walk, reintroducing the filesystem walk lib.sh exists to eliminate
findings.failure_scenario: The gate counts through `scoped_files` -> `workspace_files`, which is git-derived; the assertion counts through `Files.walk(ROOT)` filtered by three hand-written path substrings. MEASURED: with one untracked `.java` added under `ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/`, the gate printed `ok 101 business-logic file(s)` while the walk computed 102, so `assertThat(r.out()).contains(files + " business-logic file(s)")` fails -- the harness suite goes red because of an uncommitted work-in-progress file that is not part of the commit under test. The walk also does not exclude `.tmp/`, which lib.sh names by name as the scenario it exists to make unreachable ('a reference clone under .tmp/ ... unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by each gate remembering to exclude them'), and check-gate-scope.sh polices only `scripts/`, so nothing catches it here. Counting via `git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java'` in the test would assert the same number against the same source of truth.

findings.title: The exemption argument's superlative is false as measured, and it is restated in four places
findings.location: AGENTS.md (implicitly), docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md:24-26, scripts/check-io-seam.sh header, buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/IoSeamGateTest.java class javadoc, backlog.md M0.107 State cell
findings.failure_scenario: '`LocalSequencer implements Sequencer` and holds more business logic than any other file in the tree' is stated as fact in four files. MEASURED by line count over the 103 tracked src/main files: `sequencer/.../ChainReplay.java` is 604 lines and `sequencer/.../LocalSequencer.java` is 578, so LocalSequencer is not the largest business-logic file; ChainReplay is, and it implements no seam. The substance of the argument survives and is correct -- I verified that 11 src/main files match `implements .*(BinStore|Sequencer|SubscriptionTransport|Membership|Clock)`, so an `implements` carve-out would have been five times wider than the one module, and LocalSequencer is the largest of those 11 -- but the sentence as written is a superlative a reader can check and find wrong, in four copies, which is this milestone's recorded prose-defect class. 'the largest file that implements one of the five seams' is true and is the claim the argument actually needs.
